analysis: Examined the changes: a comment-only edit in ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift (head lines 70-71, capacityRefreshTick; the full file is replayed and the proactive sweep behavior is unchanged in this file). ProviderLoop+MemoryProtection.swift adds CBv2RetainedKVSegments.requestRelease() at head line 60, inside the MemoryPressureMonitor clearCache closure and after the existing native-MiMo reclamation guards (lines 56-58). That path only signals engines to drop retained free KV segments at their next step. ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift adds a countingRetainedKVSegments parameter to the reclaimable-memory arithmetic, an evictionCanReach helper, and releaseReclaimableMemoryForLoad (which calls GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments and then clearCacheAfterConfirmedNativeOwnership). The load-admission and eviction flow now releases retained segments once before evicting a model. It also re-checks the native MiMo, Nemotron and retirement refusal verdicts after the Nemotron certainty check suspends. Security-relevant observations: (1) The change reduces memory residency of free KV segments and does not touch the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041), keys, attestation, authorization or the coordinator wire contract. (2) Retained free KV segments are in-process GPU/host memory already inside the process trust boundary (T-028 residual-data class). The release path frees and drops them rather than exposing them. Whether freed segments are zeroed or overwritten is outside the supplied evidence, so the T-028 posture is unchanged. (3) Credit for retained segments is counted only as an eviction-feasibility estimate before release and is excluded after release, which avoids evicting a model for room the load never gets. This is an availability and correctness property and I found no abuse path. (4) The patch excerpt for ModelLoading is truncated, but the visible hunks are consistent. Not verified: the implementations of CBv2RetainedKVSegments, GlobalKVCacheBudget.releaseRetainedKVSegments and busyEnginesKeepReclaimableMemory, and the reentrancy implications of the new awaits in fastAdmissionReject and evictUntilAvailable, which were not supplied. I identified no concrete security regression.
